verses.104:1: Dai graças ao Senhor, e invocai o seu nome: * anunciai entre as nações as suas obras.
verses.104:2: Cantai-lhe, e entoai-lhe salmos: * narrai todas as suas maravilhas.
verses.104:3: {laudamini} no seu santo nome: * alegre-se o coração dos que buscam o Senhor.
verses.104:4: Buscai o Senhor, e {confirmamini}: * buscai sempre a sua face.
verses.104:5: Lembrai-vos das suas maravilhas, que ele fez: * dos seus prodígios, e dos juízos da sua boca.
verses.104:6: Descendência de Abraão, {servi}: * filhos de Jacó, {electi}.
verses.104:7: Ele é o Senhor, nosso Deus: * em toda a terra estão os seus juízos.
verses.104:8: Lembrou-se para sempre da sua aliança: * da palavra que ordenou para mil gerações:
verses.104:9: Que {disposuit} com Abraão: * e do seu juramento a Isaac:
verses.104:10: E a firmou para Jacó como decreto: * e para Israel como aliança eterna:
verses.104:11: Dizendo: A ti darei a terra de Canaã, * {funiculus} da vossa herança.
verses.104:12: Quando eram em pequeno número, * pouquíssimos, e forasteiros nela:
verses.104:13: E passaram de nação em nação, * e de um reino a outro povo.
verses.104:14: Não deixou que homem algum lhes fizesse mal: * e castigou reis por causa deles.
verses.104:15: Não toqueis nos meus {christos}: * e aos meus profetas não façais o mal.
verses.104:16: E chamou a fome sobre a terra: * e quebrou todo o {firmamentum} do pão.
verses.104:17: Enviou adiante deles um homem: * José foi vendido como servo.
verses.104:18: Humilharam nos grilhões os seus pés, o ferro {pertransiit} a sua alma, * até que viesse a sua palavra.
verses.104:19: {eloquium} {inflammavit}: * o rei enviou, e o soltou; o príncipe dos povos, e o deixou ir.
verses.104:21: Estabeleceu-o senhor da sua casa: * e príncipe de todos os seus bens:
verses.104:22: Para que instruísse os seus príncipes como a si mesmo: * e ensinasse a prudência aos seus anciãos.
verses.104:23: E Israel entrou no Egito: * e Jacó foi forasteiro na terra de Cam.
verses.104:24: E aumentou muito o seu povo: * e {firmavit} os seus inimigos.
verses.104:25: {convertit} o coração deles para que odiassem o seu povo: * e {dolum} os seus servos.
verses.104:26: Enviou Moisés, seu servo: * e Aarão, a quem escolheu.
verses.104:27: Pôs neles {verba} dos seus sinais: * e dos prodígios na terra de Cam.
verses.104:28: Enviou trevas, e escureceu: * e não {exacerbavit} as suas palavras.
verses.104:29: Converteu em sangue as águas deles: * e matou os peixes deles.
verses.104:30: A terra deles produziu rãs: * nos aposentos dos próprios reis deles.
verses.104:31: Disse, e veio a mosca canina: * e mosquitos em todos os seus confins.
verses.104:32: {posuit}: * fogo que queimava na terra deles.
verses.104:33: E feriu as vinhas deles, e as figueiras deles: * e quebrou as árvores dos seus confins.
verses.104:34: Disse, e veio o gafanhoto, e {bruchus}, * que não tinha número:
verses.104:35: E comeu toda a erva na terra deles: * e comeu todo o fruto da terra deles.
verses.104:36: E feriu todo primogênito na terra deles: * as primícias de todo o seu trabalho.
verses.104:37: E os {eduxit37} com prata e ouro: * e não havia enfermo nas suas tribos.
verses.104:38: Alegrou-se o Egito com a partida deles: * porque o temor deles {incubuit} sobre eles.
verses.104:39: Estendeu uma nuvem para proteção deles: * e um fogo, para lhes dar luz durante a noite.
verses.104:40: Pediram, e veio a codorniz: * e com o pão do céu os saciou.
verses.104:41: {dirupit} a rocha, e correram as águas: * {abierunt}.
verses.104:42: Porque se lembrou da sua santa palavra: * {habuit} a Abraão, seu servo.
verses.104:43: E {eduxit43} o seu povo com exultação, * e os seus escolhidos com alegria.
verses.104:44: E deu-lhes as regiões das nações: * e possuíram os trabalhos dos povos:
verses.104:45: Para que guardem os seus preceitos, * e procurem a sua lei.

decisions.why: The Latin is a passive imperative of laudáre (the Greek ἐπαινεῖσθε, middle-passive). DRB 'Glory ye' and MS1932 'Gloriai-vos' give the Greek middle's sense of boasting, which changes the verb. The glossary row laudári keeps the Latin's passive (33:3 'será louvada a minha alma', 62:12, 63:11 'serão louvados'), each time against MS1932's 'gloriar-se'. Ruled for the row: the root of praise stays and the Latin column is matched. The cost is that a passive imperative ('be praised') is rare in Portuguese; the reader may hear it as odd.

options.label: Sede louvados
options.note: Ruling: the laudári row (33:3, 62:12, 63:11). The passive is kept.

options.label: Gloriai-vos
options.note: MS1932; DRB 'Glory ye'. The Greek middle's sense. It swaps the verb for another word, so D2 refuses it as the ruling.

options.label: Louvai-vos
options.note: Keeps the root with a reflexive. It would be heard as 'praise yourselves', which is wrong.

decisions.why: The confirmáre row (open) proposes 'confirmar' only where a thing or a word is confirmed. With persons it proposes 'sustentar' or 'firmar', because the blind reader heard 'confirmar os justos' (36:17) as attesting. Here the person is the subject of a passive imperative. The Greek κραταιώθητε is 'be made strong', the same verb as 104:24 'firmávit eum' (ἐκραταίωσεν), and 'fortalecei-vos' (MS1932 'fortificai-vos') says it plainly. 'Confirmai-vos' would be heard as the sacrament. This colon is also the Saturday Matins versicle (V. Quǽrite Dóminum, et confirmámini. R. Quǽrite fáciem ejus semper — Psalmi matutinum) and the Introit verse of Quad4-4, so it must read alone.

options.label: fortalecei-vos
options.note: Ruling: the Greek's sense ('be made strong'), and MS1932's. It is safe at the vós imperative (past 'fortaleci').

options.label: firmai-vos
options.note: The row's option for persons. It is a rarer reflexive.

options.label: confirmai-vos
options.note: The cognate. It would be heard as the sacrament of Confirmation or as attesting.

decisions.latin: Semen Ábraham, servi ejus: * fílii Jacob, elécti ejus
decisions.why: 'servi ejus' and 'elécti ejus' can be nominative plural ('his servants … his chosen ones', in apposition to the people addressed) or genitive singular ('of Abraham his servant … of Jacob his chosen one'). The Latin leaves it open; Portuguese cannot. The Septuagint that the Latin renders has the plural (δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ … ἐκλεκτοὶ αὐτοῦ, Rahlfs in the parallels), and so has MS1932 ('que sois seus servos … seus escolhidos'). DRB reads the singular ('Abraham his servant … Jacob his chosen'), which is the Hebrew's. Ruled for the plural under rule 1: where the Latin follows the Septuagint, we follow the Latin as the Greek explains it. 104:42 'Ábraham, púerum suum' still calls Abraham 'seu servo'.

options.label: seus servos … seus escolhidos
options.note: Ruling: the LXX plural; MS1932.

options.label: seu servo … seu escolhido
options.note: DRB: the genitive singular, Abraham and Jacob as the servant and the chosen one.

decisions.why: dispónere of a covenant is διατίθημι (διέθετο). At 82:6 'testaméntum disposuérunt' took 'firmaram aliança', the ordináre testaméntum verb (D44). But the next verse has statúere, whose row is 'firmar' (104:10 'E a firmou para Jacó'), and the Greek there is another verb (ἔστησεν). If both were 'firmar', two Latin verbs and two Greek verbs would become one Portuguese verb in adjacent lines. So dispónere takes 'fazer … com', the plain Portuguese of making a covenant (DRB 'which he made to Abraham', MS1932 'que fez a Abraão'). The relative 'Que' stays as open as the Latin's neuter 'quod', which may point back to the word or the covenant.

options.label: fez
options.note: Ruling: DRB, MS1932. It leaves 'firmar' to statúere in the next verse.

options.label: firmou
options.note: 82:6's verb for the same Greek. It would give 'firmou … firmou' across 104:9–10 for two Latin verbs.

options.label: dispôs
options.note: The cognate. 'dispor com Abraão' is not said.

decisions.why: funículus is the measuring cord (L&S 'a slender rope, a cord'; σχοίνισμα, the portion measured by line). Ps 77:54b kept the cord in 'com a corda da distribuição' (funículo distributiónis). The concrete image stays (rule 5). MS1932 'como porção da tua herança' and DRB 'the lot' explain it. The switch from 'A ti' (tibi) to 'vossa' (vestræ) is the Latin's own, and so is its number (God speaks to one patriarch, then to the people). It is kept under D17.

options.label: a corda
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's image, as 77:54b.

options.label: a porção
options.note: MS1932. It explains the image and loses the cord.

options.label: o lote
options.note: DRB 'the lot'. The same loss.

decisions.why: D19 gave the singular Christus 'Cristo' and said that the plural 104:15 cannot follow and will want 'ungidos'. 'Os meus cristos' would be heard as images of Christ, or as a slip. 'ungidos' keeps the anointing (χριστοί), and MS1932 has it. 'Tocar em' is the Brazilian construction.

options.label: ungidos
options.note: Ruling: as D19 foresaw; MS1932.

options.label: cristos
options.note: The Latin's word. In Portuguese the plural is heard as crucifixes.

decisions.why: D31 made firmaméntum 'esteio' where it is a support and 'firmamento' where it is the sky, and left 104:16 to be decided here. This place is a support: στήριγμα ἄρτου, bread as the staff that holds a man up. So the verse takes D31's word. The prop is broken, and 'quebrou' is contérere's verb, as in 104:33. MS1932's 'sustento' explains the image and loses it.

options.label: esteio
options.note: Ruling: D31 (support), the image kept.

options.label: sustento
options.note: MS1932. Plainer, but it names the effect and not the prop.

options.label: apoio
options.note: DRB 'support'.

decisions.latin: ferrum pertránsiit ánimam ejus (cf. 104:13 pertransiérunt de gente in gentem)
decisions.why: One Latin verb twice in the psalm (διέρχομαι both times). At 104:13 it is going from nation to nation, and 'passaram' is the only natural word. Here the iron goes through a soul, and 'passou pela sua alma' is weak. 'traspassou' is MS1932's word and the plain Portuguese for a blade through the body. It keeps 'passar' inside it, so the ear still hears the root. The Latin is also heard with the sword of Simeon's prophecy (Lk 2:35 in the Vulgate has 'pertransibit gladius' — from memory, unverified). The word order 'Humilharam nos grilhões os seus pés' keeps the Latin's image of humbled feet, which MS1932 turns into 'Humilharam-no com grilhões nos pés'.

options.label: traspassou
options.note: Ruling: MS1932; the blade's verb.

options.label: atravessou
options.note: Plainer. With it 104:13 could read 'atravessaram' to keep one verb.

options.label: passou através de
options.note: The verb of 104:13 exactly. Flat and long.

decisions.why: D16 and D26 made elóquium the clause 'o que dissestes' and said that outside Ps 118 the psalm decides where there is a genitive or a subject. The previous verse ends on verbum ('até que viesse a sua palavra'), and the Greek has λόγος there and λόγιον here, so D15's test keeps them apart. 'A palavra do Senhor' would merge them in adjacent colons. The clause keeps the distinction in the D26 form, with the Lord named in place of 'vós'. 'O dito do Senhor' is the noun D16 held in reserve, but the stylist refused 'dito' in every place he met it.

options.label: O que o Senhor disse
options.note: Ruling: D26's clause, the third person.

options.label: O dito do Senhor
options.note: The noun D16 allows where a genitive needs one.

options.label: A palavra do Senhor
options.note: MS1932, DRB. It merges elóquium with the verbum of the line before.

decisions.why: The inflammáre row (96:3 'queimar', where fire burns the enemies) said that 104:19 decides by its object. Here the object is Joseph and the subject a word. The Greek ἐπύρωσεν is 'refined by fire, tried'. The Latin says 'set on fire'. DRB 'inflamed him' and MS1932 'o tinha inflamado' keep the cognate, which in Portuguese is heard as kindled or roused. The Latin leaves open whether it means trial or ardour, and so does 'inflamou'. 'Queimou' would be heard as harm, and 'provou no fogo' is the Greek's explanation.

options.label: o inflamou
options.note: Ruling: DRB, MS1932; the Latin's own word.

options.label: o queimou
options.note: 96:3's verb. With a person and a word it is heard as harm.

options.label: o provou no fogo
options.note: The Greek ἐπύρωσεν explained. It says more than the Latin.

decisions.latin: et firmávit eum super inimícos ejus
decisions.why: firmáre here is κραταιόω, 'made strong', the Greek of 104:4 'confirmámini' (fortalecei-vos). 'super' + accusative with a verb of strength means beyond, stronger than (ὑπέρ). 'o firmou sobre os seus inimigos' is not a Portuguese sentence. 'o fez mais forte que' says the Latin's sense in the grammar Portuguese has, and keeps the root 'forte' that 104:4 has in 'fortalecei-vos'. This colon is also the second Saturday Matins antiphon ('Auxit Dóminus * pópulum suum: et firmávit eum super inimícos ejus'), and each half reads alone.

options.label: o fez mais forte que
options.note: Ruling: the Greek ὑπέρ as a comparative; the root of 104:4.

options.label: o tornou forte sobre
options.note: MS1932 'tornou-o forte sobre'. It keeps 'super'.

options.label: o fortaleceu sobre
options.note: The verb of 104:4 exactly. The preposition is strained.

decisions.latin: Convértit cor eórum ut odírent pópulum ejus
decisions.why: The convértere row gives 'voltar' when the sense is turning back or towards, and 'converter em' only when one thing is changed into another (104:29 'Converteu em sangue'). Here a heart is turned towards hatred, so the row's verb stands. MS1932's 'Mudou' says change of mind, which is plainer but is another verb.

options.label: Voltou
options.note: Ruling: the convértere row.

options.label: Mudou
options.note: MS1932. Plainer. It is another verb.

decisions.latin: et dolum fácerent in servos ejus
decisions.why: dolus → engano (row). The light verb 'fácere dolum' has one precedent: 51:4 'fecísti dolum' → 'tramaste o engano' (D44 notes it as the one place 'tramar' renders fácere). Following it keeps the noun the Latin has and gives Portuguese a real verb for it. The Greek is one verb here (δολιοῦσθαι), and 5:11a let the light verb go in that case ('enganavam'), which is the option. 'in servos' → 'contra', the hostile sense of 'in'.

options.label: tramassem engano contra
options.note: Ruling: 51:4's build; the noun kept.

options.label: enganassem
options.note: 5:11a's build for the one Greek verb. Shorter; the noun is lost.

options.label: usassem de engano com
options.note: MS1932 'usassem de enganos com'.

decisions.latin: Pósuit in eis verba signórum suórum
decisions.why: The Latin (= the Greek τοὺς λόγους τῶν σημείων) has 'the words of his signs'. It is a Hebraism for 'the matters, the deeds' of the signs. Most readers take 'in eis' as Moses and Aaron. DRB ('He gave them power to shew his signs') and MS1932 ('Deu-lhes poder para fazer milagres') explain it. The words are kept, and so is 'Pôs', which echoes 77:43 'Como pôs no Egito os seus sinais'. The ambiguity of 'neles' (the two brothers, or the Egyptians among whom the signs were set) is left open as the Latin leaves it.

options.label: as palavras
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word (verbum → palavra, D15).

options.label: o poder de mostrar
options.note: DRB and MS1932's explanation. It supplies what the Latin does not say.

decisions.why: The most obscure colon of the psalm. The Greek has no 'not' and a plural verb ('they provoked his words'). The Latin has 'non' and a singular: 'he did not embitter his words' (DRB 'grieved not his words'). MS1932 gives up and paraphrases ('não faltou nenhuma das suas palavras'). D27 settled 'provocar' for exacerbáre where it stands alone with God as object. Here the object is words, and 'não provocou as suas palavras' is not a Portuguese sentence. The cognate 'exacerbar' is current in Brazil (to make harsher, to aggravate). It keeps the Latin's word and its obscurity, and it lets the reader hear either 'did not make his words harsher' or the traditional sense that the plagues did not overshoot his word. 'as suas palavras' is sermo → palavra (D15).

options.label: exacerbou
options.note: Ruling: the cognate, which is current Portuguese. Local, because the object is not God.

options.label: provocou
options.note: D27's verb for God as object. It gives no sense with 'palavras'.

options.label: tornou amargas
options.note: The root acerbus; DRB's 'grieved'. It explains.

decisions.why: pónere with two accusatives, 'made their rains hail'. 'Fez das chuvas deles granizo' is the Portuguese of 'pónere X Y' ('fazer de X Y'), and it keeps the rains and the hail in the Latin's order. 'Pôs' cannot take two objects. DRB ('He gave them hail for rain') and MS1932 ('Em vez de água fez-lhes chover granizo') rebuild the verse. The second colon keeps the participle comburéntem as a relative clause ('que queimava'). 'abrasador' (MS1932) was unknown to the Ps 96 reader.

options.label: Fez das chuvas deles granizo
options.note: Ruling: the double accusative in Portuguese form.

options.label: Deu-lhes granizo em vez de chuva

forms.posuit: Deu-lhes granizo em vez de chuva

options.note: DRB's build. The possessive 'eórum' is lost.

options.label: Converteu as chuvas deles em granizo

forms.posuit: Converteu as chuvas deles em granizo

options.note: Clear, but it borrows convértere's verb from 104:29.

decisions.why: bruchus (βροῦχος) is, in L&S, 'a kind of locust without wings': the young locust before its wings. 'gafanhoto' is locústa's word (77:46). Portuguese has the learned 'bruco', which almost no one knows. 'lagarta' is a crawling, crop-eating larva, the nearest common word. MS1932's 'lagartos' (lizards) is a slip or a misprint, and DRB keeps 'bruchus'. A named creature is kept concrete (rule 5).

options.label: a lagarta
options.note: Ruling: the common word for the crawling crop-eater.

options.label: o bruco
options.note: The cognate. Exact, but a dictionary word.

options.label: o gafanhoto sem asas
options.note: L&S's gloss. It explains, and repeats 'gafanhoto'.

decisions.latin: Et edúxit eos … Et edúxit pópulum suum
decisions.why: One verb twice in the psalm. The edúcere row gives 'fazer sair', and 'tirar de' where a source is named. Ps 77:52 'Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum' is another verb, but the Ps 77 translation used 'tirou' for edúcere at 77:16 ('E tirou água da rocha'). This psalm's narrative is kept in Ps 77's vocabulary, as asked. 'tirou' is short and plain, and 'E tirou o seu povo com exultação' reads alone as the third Saturday Matins antiphon ('Edúxit Deus * pópulum suum in exsultatióne'). 'fez sair' is the row's form and the option.

options.label: tirou … tirou
options.note: Ruling: Ps 77:16's verb for edúcere.

options.label: fez sair … fez sair
options.note: The edúcere row; MS1932 at 104:37 ('fez sair os Israelitas').

decisions.latin: quia incúbuit timor eórum super eos
decisions.why: incúmbere is 'to lie upon, press upon, weigh upon' (L&S). The Greek ἐπέπεσεν is 'fell upon'. The Latin's image is weight, so 'pesava' is the ruling. The double 'deles … eles' (fear of the Israelites upon the Egyptians) is the Latin's 'eórum … eos'. It is kept, and so is the ambiguity; MS1932 explains it ('por causa do grande temor que lhe causavam').

options.label: pesava
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's image of weight.

options.label: tinha caído
options.note: The Greek ἐπέπεσεν.

decisions.why: Ps 77:15 'Interrúpit petram' → 'Fendeu a rocha'. The Greek of both verses is one verb (διέρρηξεν πέτραν), so D15's test would allow one Portuguese verb. But the Latin verb differs, and dirúmpere has its own row ('romper', Ps 2:3, where the Greek is the same διαρρήγνυμι). As at 77:40, the Latin verb rules. 'fluxérunt aquæ' is identical Latin to 77:20 and has identical Portuguese: 'e correram as águas'.

options.label: Rompeu
options.note: Ruling: the dirúmpere row.

options.label: Fendeu
options.note: Ps 77:15's word for the same Greek; MS1932 'Fendeu a pedra'.

decisions.why: abíre is 'go off, go away'; the Greek ἐπορεύθησαν is 'went, journeyed' (ἐν ἀνύδροις, in waterless places). 'correr' is taken by 'fluxérunt' in the first colon, so the rivers need their own verb of going. 'seguiram' is 'went on their way', and 'in sicco' → 'pela terra seca' (65:6 'em terra seca'). The bare 'foram' is barred because it is also 'they were'. The Latin's asyndeton after the mediant is kept.

options.label: rios seguiram pela terra seca
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: correram rios em lugar seco
options.note: MS1932. Plain, but 'correram' twice for two Latin verbs.

options.label: rios iam pelo lugar seco
options.note: The Greek's 'went'; the imperfect is weak.

decisions.latin: quod hábuit ad Ábraham, púerum suum
decisions.why: 'the word which he had towards Abraham' (τοῦ πρὸς Αβρααμ). The Saturday Matins versicle rewrites it as 'Quod locútus est ad Ábraham', which shows how the Office heard it. 'que dirigiu a Abraão' is the Portuguese idiom for words addressed to someone ('dirigir a palavra a'), and it stays close to the vague 'hábuit ad'. MS1932's 'que tinha dado' leans to promise. púer → 'servo': the Greek is τὸν δοῦλον, the word behind servus in 104:6 and 104:26, so D15 merges them; 'menino' would be wrong.

options.label: que dirigiu
options.note: Ruling: the idiom of an addressed word.

options.label: que tinha dado
options.note: MS1932. 'dar a palavra' is to promise, which is more than hábuit says.

options.label: que teve para com
options.note: The Latin word for word. Heavy.

choices.104:1: D5 (Dai graças), invocáre → invocar, annuntiáre → anunciar (D41), gentes → nações. The Latin's order, 'entre as nações as suas obras', ends on the object.
choices.104:2: psállere → entoar salmos (D25), the dative 'ei' as 'lhe' in both verbs, as the Latin repeats it.
choices.104:5: judícia → juízos (D15); 'que ele fez' names the subject hidden in 'fecit' (D2).
choices.104:7: The copula 'estão' is supplied in the second colon (D2); 'Ipse' → 'Ele'. univérsus → 'toda' (row).
choices.104:8: in sǽculum → para sempre (D23); testaméntum → aliança (row); mandáre with a thing as object → ordenar (the mandáre row, 32:9, 118:138). The first Saturday Matins antiphon ('Memor fuit in sǽculum * testaménti sui Dóminus Deus noster') reads 'Lembrou-se para sempre da sua aliança o Senhor, nosso Deus'.
choices.104:10: statúere → firmar (row); præcéptum → decreto (D19). The feminine 'a' takes up 'palavra' / 'aliança' (the Latin's neuter 'illud' points to verbum). ætérnus → eterna.
choices.104:13: gens → nação (42:1 keeps 'gente' out); 'de nação em nação' is the Portuguese idiom of 'de gente in gentem'.
choices.104:14: corrípere → castigar (D21); nocére → fazer mal (88:23 row). 'pro eis' → 'por causa deles', since 'por eles' would be heard as agent.
choices.104:15: malignári → não façais o mal (the malignári row named this verse). The Latin's order is kept in the second colon so that the verse is a chiasm, as it is in Latin, and ends on 'mal'.
choices.104:17: servus → servo, so that Joseph, Moses (104:26), Abraham (104:42) and the seed (104:6) carry one word, as they do in Latin. 'escravo' (MS1932) is the idiom for a man sold, but it would break that repetition.
choices.104:18: One mediant only, as in the Latin; the first colon is long, as the Latin's is. 'a sua palavra' leaves open whose word it is (Joseph's interpretation or God's), as 'verbum ejus' does.
choices.104:19: DO joins Vulgate 104:19b–20 in one prayed verse (no 104:20 id). misit → 'enviou', one verb with 104:17, 26, 28; the king's missing object is left missing, as in DRB. dimíttere (let go) → deixar ir (row). "o rei enviou" keeps rex as the subject; "enviou o rei" would be heard as the king being sent.
choices.104:21: constitúere → estabelecer (row); posséssio (goods) → bens, as 77:48 v2.
choices.104:22: erudíre → instruir (row); docére → ensinar (row); senes → anciãos (row). 'como a si mesmo' keeps the Latin's open reference.
choices.104:23: áccola (πάροικος, the Greek of íncola) → forasteiro, by D39's merge. Cham → Cam (77:51).
choices.104:26: 'e' is supplied before Aarão. Without it the second name is heard as an apposition to Moses (grammar, D2). Móyses, Aaron → Moisés, Aarão (row).
choices.104:29: convértere in → converter em (row); the Latin's order is changed to 77:44's ('converteu em sangue os rios deles') so that the two tellings of the plague sound alike. The rhyme flag on "deles … deles" (104:29, 35, 38, and 29/30) is the Latin's own eórum repeated; it is accepted, as in Ps 77.
choices.104:30: penetrália → aposentos (inner rooms); MS1932's 'câmaras' is heard as a legislature in Brazil. 'ipsórum' → 'próprios'.
choices.104:31: cœnomyía → a mosca canina (77:45 row); cínifes (σκνῖπες, gnats) → mosquitos (MS1932); fines → confins (row).
choices.104:33: lignum → árvore (row), the collective singular made plural (grammar). contérere → quebrar, as 104:16.
choices.104:34: 'cujus non erat númerus' → 'que não tinha número': the number kept (D41 kept 'número' in 'além de todo número').
choices.104:35: fænum → erva (the row's split: here grass is eaten growing, not dried as hay). The repeated 'comeu' is the Latin's.
choices.104:36: Identical to 77:51 wherever the Latin is identical: 'E feriu todo primogênito … as primícias de todo o seu trabalho' (rule 6).
choices.104:39: protéctio → proteção (row); 'per noctem' → 'durante a noite' (91:3). lucére is 'to give light', not illumináre ('iluminar').
choices.104:40: cotúrnix: the Latin's collective singular kept ('veio a codorniz'), which echoes 'veio a mosca canina … veio o gafanhoto'. saturáre → saciar (row); 'pão do céu' = 77:24.
choices.104:43: in + ablative of manner → 'com' (as 99:2); exsultátio → exultação, lætítia → alegria (row). Reads alone as the Saturday Matins antiphon.
choices.104:44: labóres → trabalhos, the fruit of toil (77:46, 77:51); possidére → possuir (row).
choices.104:45: justificatiónes → preceitos (D15; this is its one place outside Ps 118); requírere → procurar (row). Present subjunctive, as the Latin.

audit.note: Draft 1 from the parallels (Latin, LXX, DRB, MS1932; no DM1962 for this psalm), and from Ps 77's prayed text for every shared phrase. Ps 105 is not in this worktree, so it could not be compared. The hard readings: 104:6 (servi ejus: plural or genitive), 104:19 (elóquium beside verbum), 104:27 (verba signórum), 104:28 (non exacerbávit sermónes), 104:41 (abiérunt in sicco). The Saturday Matins antiphons and versicles from this psalm (Psalmi matutinum [Day6], [Daym6C]) and the Introit verse (Quad4-4, 093-5) were read in DO so that those colons read alone.

Hard checks pass. Length flags accepted (the long colons follow the Latin sense; 104:9 "Que fez com Abraão" is short as the Latin is). The rhyme flags on "deles" are the Latin's eórum and are accepted. 104:30 punctuation brought back to the Latin's colon.
